# authwise_domain_activation (Resource)

Waits until a custom host (`authwise_domain`) routes: `PROVISIONING` or `ACTIVE`, its certificate issued and attached to the hostname. Put it between the domain's two DNS records, with `depends_on` naming the challenge record, and make the traffic record depend on it. One apply then creates the domain and the challenge record, waits for the certificate, and only then points traffic at the hostname, so no request ever meets a missing certificate.

It does not wait for `ACTIVE`. Authwise confirms `ACTIVE` by finding the traffic record in public DNS, so the domain reaches it on the controller's next check once the traffic record has propagated, after this resource is created. `state` says which of the two it saw.

It manages nothing in Authwise. Destroying it only removes it from state; a domain that leaves `ACTIVE` later (`DEGRADED`) is not replaced.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# login.acme.com's activation, between its two DNS records.
resource "authwise_domain" "login" {
  issuer_id = authwise_issuer.main.issuer_id
  hostname  = "login.acme.com"
}

locals {
  login_records = { for r in authwise_domain.login.dns_records : r.purpose => r }
}

resource "cloudflare_record" "login_challenge" {
  zone_id = var.zone_id
  name    = local.login_records["challenge"].name
  type    = local.login_records["challenge"].type
  content = local.login_records["challenge"].value

  # DNS-only. Proxied, Cloudflare would stand in front of Authwise, which
  # is not supported, and the certificate authority could not see the
  # challenge record.
  proxied = false
}

resource "authwise_domain_activation" "login" {
  domain     = authwise_domain.login.name
  depends_on = [cloudflare_record.login_challenge]
}

resource "cloudflare_record" "login_traffic" {
  zone_id = var.zone_id
  name    = local.login_records["traffic"].name
  type    = local.login_records["traffic"].type
  content = local.login_records["traffic"].value
  proxied = false

  depends_on = [authwise_domain_activation.login]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The domain's full resource name, `authwise_domain.<name>.name`. Changing it, as replacing the domain does, waits again.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `certificate_expires_at` (String) When the domain's current certificate expires, RFC 3339.
- `hostname` (String) The domain's hostname.
- `state` (String) The domain's state as last read: `PROVISIONING` or `ACTIVE` once created, and whatever it is now after a refresh.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the domain's full resource name. Importing does not wait.
terraform import authwise_domain_activation.login tenants/t-01/domains/d-01
```
